Market insiders report that the cathode import premium has risen to around an average of $70/t. Some have said that business has improved sufficiently for them to achieve $80/tonne. Others are a bit less optimistic, saying that sellers are quoting $80/t and buyers are offering $40-50/tonne, with deals being struck at around $60/t. In general we can say that the import premium is in a $60-80/tonne range. SXEW cathode is being quoted around $10/t lower at $50-70/tonne. © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** **June 2012** www.crugroup.com Stocks in the bonded warehouses in Shanghai fell again over the past two weeks, mainly attributed to higher exports. The stocks in the bonded warehouses in Shanghai are estimated at 500,000t and in Nanhai at around 50,000t. There have been news stories that some market insiders Chinese expect exports of refined copper will total 110,000t in May and June. This would be the highest ever 2-month total, beating the 81,363t exported in March and April last year. This seems optimistic, though, as LME Asian warehouses have registered only a 43,250t increase from the recent 8th May low point. This rise in exports is partly due to the short positions of Chinese smelters on the LME. The backwardation on the LME had prompted them to announce they will export enough cathode to cover their positions. Subsequently, the backwardation between the cash and 3-month contracts on the LME had narrowed to a flat position as of 7th June. Thus, exports for the remainder of June are likely to only be as a result of lags due to shipping times. The nearby LME warehouses are still seeing rising inflows of metal, principally into Busan. # More details on recently announced subsidy schemes 

The detailed policy on the subsidy schemes was issued for flat panel TV and air conditioners on 28<sup>th</sup> May and the policy for refrigerators, washing machines and water heaters was released on 4<sup>th</sup> June, as presented in the table below. 

|**Products**|**Subsidy (Rmb/unit)**|
|---|---|
|LED TV|100-400|
|Plasma TV|250-400|
|Fixed frequency air conditioner|180-330|
|Variable frequency air conditioner|240-400|
|Refrigerator|70-400|
|Washing machine|100-600|

We take the view that the subsidy for energy efficient products will help support the weak demand for white goods in China.  However, the impact from the policy would be limited in generating new sales compared with the “scrappage” and “white goods going to the countryside” schemes that followed in the wake of the financial crisis.  “The white goods going to the country side” policy generated huge new demand for air-conditioners and refrigerators because people in rural areas generally did not have these home appliances before.  The scrappage scheme also generated new demand because those who had used old refrigerators for many years would like to have new ones and took advantage of the scheme.  However, the subsidy for energy efficient products is for those who plan to buy new ones.  Given the previous schemes brought forward a great deal of demand, it is uncertain how much demand will be generated, or if there will only be a shift towards more energy efficient ones and therefore only a modest impact on copper consumption. 

# China reiterates macro control over the property market 

Due to the recent slowdown in the Chinese economy, many in the market expected that the Chinese government might slightly loosen macro control over the property market in an effort to ensure growth. However, on 5<sup>th</sup> June the spokesman for MOHURD (Ministry of Housing and Urban Rural Development) stressed that China will strictly implement the macro control policy, while at the same time China will speed up the construction of 7M units of social housing.  The latter is likely to support copper demand from the construction sector this year.  According to the National Statistics Bureau, the investment in the property market totalled RMB1.58 trillion i

The official LME cash copper price fell below US$7,300/t on 8th June, its lowest level since 20th December 2011. The cash-to-3 month backwardation narrowed to parity over the past two weeks, as metal was delivered into LME warehouses. The price decline was due to Eurozone fears and disappointment that the US Federal Reserve is not likely to instigate any new stimulus measures. © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 4 **June 2012** www.crugroup.com As for SHFE prices, the backwardation has remained, with the physical market price averaging over RMB300/t above the SHFE cash-month price and the cash-month to 3-month backwardation averaging a further RMB685/t for the past two weeks. This is attributed mainly to a tightening of physical availability through lower imports and restrained domestic refined production growth, as demand growth has been relatively poor. There have been some news reports of consumer restocking, but we do not believe this to be significant. Unlike the LME, the backwardation on SHFE has not attracted metal to the exchange. The decline in cathode inventory in SHFE warehouses continued, down by 25,068t over the past two weeks. The further correction in the high inventory level supports our view that imports of cathode are still declining and traders are going to SHFE for metal. We expect that with the arbitrage window narrowing, Chinese refined copper exports should fall back next month. We expect that copper prices on SHFE will continue to react to LME and macroeconomic developments and trade in a RMB50,000-55,000/t range over the middle two weeks of June. ### **Questions or comments may be addressed to:** **Wan Ling (Beijing):** +86 10 6510 2183 ling.wan@crugroup.com **Paul Settles (London):** +44 20 7903 2227 paul.settles@crugroup.com This issue was completed on 8th June 2012.
